title: Paris protesters demonstrate against living costs and police powers bill
seoTitle: Paris cost-of-living and police bill rally

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated over surging living costs, public service cuts, and a new parliamentary bill expanding police powers and weapon use.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded better learning conditions, children's rights, the rejection of the police protection bill, and higher wages.
tea.changed: Nov 16: Unions called for a nationwide general strike after the government announced a basic wage hike.

summary: Demonstrators took to the streets in Paris and across France for the fifth consecutive weekend to protest against high living costs, public service cuts, and a proposed parliamentary bill that would give police greater legal protection when using weapons. Organised in part by students, unions, and Yellow Vest activists, the movement saw varying turnout figures, with the interior minister reporting 106,000 participants nationwide including 24,000 in Paris, while student unions claimed 200,000 total participants with nearly 100,000 in the capital. Protesters chanted slogans against the president and the police. In response to the unrest, the government announced basic wage increases and low-wage talks, though unions dismissed these measures as insufficient and called for a nationwide general strike.
demands: Lower living costs and raise wages
response: According to the sources, the government announced a 1.6% basic wage increase starting in December and initiated a month-long low-wage consultation with unions, though unions criticised the steps as inadequate and called for a general strike.

crowd.text: Student unions put the number of demonstrators at 200,000, including almost 100,000 in the capital.

updates.text: Demonstrators marched in Paris and other cities for the fifth consecutive Saturday over living costs and police bills.
The public accounts minister stated that increasing the public sector minimum wage would benefit 1.35 million workers.
Major unions called for a nationwide general strike following government wage announcements.
